accuracy.evidence: Every number checked by hand and in the lab code: 37 lies between 30 and 40 and is 13 from 50 but 37 from 0, so 'closest to 50' is right; 346 lies between 300 and 400, before 500; the jar holds exactly 42 beads (cells.slice(0,42)) and the 10 ringed beads are about a quarter of them; 3 hundreds + 4 tens + 6 ones = 300 + 40 + 6 = 346; match rounds 2-0-5 = 205, 1-7-0 = 170, 4-0-3 = 403. Placement tolerances (±2 on 0-100, ±20 on 0-1000) suit 'approximately the right position' in the topic evidence. Curriculum wording checked against NC 2013 Year 2 number and place value ('identify, represent and estimate numbers using different representations, including the number line') and Year 3 (to 1000). Parameterised items checked at range corners: p2 100h + 10t + o (100..999), p3 m (5..50, line to 2m), p5 10t, m2 100h, m5 100h + o (101..909).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early number-line and place-value errors (Siegler & Opfer 2003 on logarithmic-style placement of small numbers; NCETM Year 2/3 place-value guidance on zero as a place holder): placing 37 near 0 because it 'feels small' (step 1 prediction '0', challenge tag small); putting any three-digit number near the end of 0-1000 (step 2 prediction, tags digit and ten, m3); reading 346 as 34 (step 2 option 'at 34'); writing 2 hundreds and 5 ones as 25 or 250 (step 5, tags zero and swap, m1, m5); swapping tens and ones (m7, swap); confusing the value of the tens digit (step 4 prediction, tags ones and hund, p5); and treating an estimate as a wild guess or something that must be counted (step 3 prediction '10'/'100', tags one and exact, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnline links three representations of one number: an open-ish number line with only start, middle and end labelled (place 37 and 346 by benchmark), a bead jar estimated from 10 ringed beads with a count-to-check, a base-ten mat whose pointer moves along a 0-1000 line as blocks are added, and a blocks-to-numeral match that hinges on zero place holders. flag3digit names the place of each digit, flagestm rounds for estimating sums, flagroundnl rounds on a line, flagm100 builds only hundreds; none places numbers by benchmark or estimates a quantity. 6-shingle similarity is at most 7.1% (with flagscale) against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds each idea before the text names it: the flag is judged on release and feedback points to the middle ('37 is less than 50, so it goes before the middle'); on 0-1000 the learner meets the same halfway reasoning with hundreds; the estimate is only accepted after 'Count to check' reveals 42, so a guess of 10 or 70 gets 'too few/too many' with the quarter-of-the-jar reason; each added block moves the pointer on the 0-1000 line so hundreds visibly make big hops and ones tiny ones; picking 25 for 2 flats and 5 cubes gets 'only two digits, put 0 where a place is empty'.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 37 is closest to '0' (the green mark lands just before 50); 346 goes 'near the end, it is a big number' or 'at 34' (it sits before 500); the jar holds 'about 10' or 'about 100' (count shows 42); 346 needs '3' or '6' tens rods (the mat needs 4); 2 hundreds and 5 ones is '25' or '250' (only 205 is accepted).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct wrong-answer messages, each naming the slip: small (48 is nearly 50, not near 0), big (48 is less than 50), zero (needs a 0 for no tens), swap (370 has 7 tens), one (10 beads are only a quarter of the jar), exact (an estimate does not need counting), digit (700 is 7 hundreds, past 500), ten (70 is 7 tens, not 700), ones (the 4 is in the tens place), hund (the 3 is the hundreds), ten2 (10 is near the start), end (100 is the end, not the middle).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes (family audience): kid text FK 1.6 (limit 5.0), adult FK 5.2 (limit 10.0). Ages 6-8 wording: short sentences, everyday words (middle, a bit before, groups of 10, close guess), curriculum terms introduced plainly (numeral via 'write it: 346', hundreds/tens/ones, flats/rods/cubes, estimate = good close guess). Lab text is one to three short sentences per step; buttons are short (+ 1 ten, More, Count to check).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap with every lesson under 12%). Kid paragraphs: three representations and zero place holder; 0-100 line with the middle; 0-1000 line; estimating from a group of 10. Adult paragraphs: curriculum statement and key words; named common mistakes; why number-line placement matters and benchmarks; what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px, dark and light), a 360 px Android viewport (light and dark) and desktop before and after Show me on all six steps. First pass had hundreds flats 32 px wide, flats stacked so three looked like one, a dashed ring around the 10 beads that also enclosed others, and labels overlapping the jar at 360 px; fixed with flats three to a row sized to the column, a ring on each of the 10 beads, and the estimate labels moved beside the jar. Numeral cards are at least 72 px tall; flag and estimate drags work anywhere on the line; control buttons wrap.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: ◀◀/◀/▶/▶▶ with aria-labels such as 'Move the flag left 10', Fewer/More/Count to check, + 1 hundred/− 1 hundred and the same for tens and ones, and one button per numeral card ('Choose 205'); challenge answers are 'Answer: …' buttons. speak() updates the canvas aria-label and the visible narration after every action ('3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones make 346'). walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes, no console errors. Canvas words sit on light cards with dark ink in both themes.
